top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Money and diplomacy drove Monday: Washington joined Tokyo in a rare coordinated yen-buying intervention, the first since 2011, while Trump's claim that Iran talks start today met a flat denial from Tehran. The Middle East stayed violent anyway, with Israeli strikes continuing in Gaza. Asia carried the rest: a record Korean heatwave, Malaysia's opposition sweeping Negeri Sembilan, and Aung San Suu Kyi seen by outsiders for the first time in 2.5 years.

stories.headline: Japan and US confirm rare joint yen-buying intervention, signal more to come
stories.summary: Japan's finance ministry and the US Treasury both confirmed a coordinated yen-buying operation aimed at what Tokyo called excessive volatility and disorderly moves in the currency, which had slid to fresh multi-decade lows. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said Japan "will not hesitate to conduct further coordinated intervention", and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington would likewise not hesitate to join further joint action. It is the first joint Japan-US currency intervention since the coordinated move that followed Japan's 2011 earthquake.

stories.headline: Iran denies Trump's claim that new talks begin on Monday
stories.summary: Iranian officials rejected US President Donald Trump's statement, made aboard Air Force One over the weekend, that negotiations with Tehran would start on Monday. Trump had said he was holding off on further strikes and had set no deadline for a deal covering the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran says no such talks were agreed. The two accounts have not been reconciled, and US embassies across the region are still advising Americans to consider departing.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill 18 in Gaza; minister says no deal obliges a halt
stories.summary: Palestinian health officials said Israeli air strikes across Gaza killed at least 18 people, the third consecutive day of strikes since the Hamas disarmament framework was announced. Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen said no agreement requires Israel to stop attacks. Hamas has said Israel must halt strikes and pull troops back before it hands over weapons. Casualty figures come from Gaza's health authorities and are not independently verified.

stories.headline: Israel conveys 'concerns' to US over the Gaza disarmament plan
stories.summary: Israel has passed formal concerns to Washington about the US-brokered framework for Hamas's disarmament and a phased Israeli withdrawal, CNA reported. An Israeli official said last week that troops would not pull back without "genuine" Hamas disarmament. The exchange leaves the plan's sequencing, and who moves first, unresolved.

stories.headline: Ukraine says Russian oil refinery and bomber airfield hit; Moscow reports eight deaths
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said overnight drone strikes hit the Saratov oil refinery, the Engels strategic bomber airfield and a fuel depot in Kaluga region. Russian regional governors reported at least eight people killed, including deaths in Belgorod and in Udmurtia some 1,300km from the front. Russia's defence ministry said it intercepted 635 drones. Claims from both sides remain independently unverified.

stories.headline: Aung San Suu Kyi meets Red Cross official in first confirmed outside contact in 2.5 years
stories.summary: Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi met an official from the International Committee of the Red Cross and appeared to be in good health, in the first confirmed contact with anyone outside the prison system in about two and a half years. She has been held since the 2021 military coup.

stories.headline: Sudanese army drone strike on court session killed 35, rights group says
stories.summary: A human rights group says a Sudanese army drone strike hit a court session, killing 35 people. The figure is the rights group's and has not been independently confirmed; the army has not published its own account of the incident.

stories.headline: Record heatwave spreads across the Korean peninsula, prompting emergency response
stories.summary: Authorities in both South and North Korea have activated emergency heat measures as an extreme heatwave grips the peninsula. South Korea recorded its highest-ever temperature of 42.5°C on 2 August, breaking the national record.

stories.headline: Two workers killed in blast after re-entering quake-hit Japanese mall
stories.summary: Two workers died in an explosion after re-entering a shopping mall damaged by the recent earthquake in southern Japan, reportedly on their employer's instruction. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi visited the quake-hit Kumamoto region on Monday as cleanup began in intense summer heat.

stories.headline: Malaysia's BN-PN sweep Negeri Sembilan; the two now eye an electoral pact for Melaka
stories.summary: Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional rode strong Malay-Muslim support to a supermajority in the Negeri Sembilan state election, and UMNO's Ismail Lasim was appointed chief minister. The two coalitions say they will begin talks soon on an electoral pact for the Melaka polls, adding to the pressure on Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's Pakatan Harapan.

stories.headline: China tightens protection for chip designs in revised regulations
stories.summary: Beijing has revised its regulations to strengthen legal protection for integrated-circuit layout designs, CNA reported. The change lands amid continuing US-China friction over semiconductor technology and export controls.

stories.headline: Alibaba unveils its largest AI model yet as DeepSeek pushes costs lower
stories.summary: Alibaba has released its biggest AI model to date, while DeepSeek's latest release is pitched at an ultra-low price point. The two announcements underline how quickly Chinese labs are competing on both scale and cost.

stories.headline: Jakarta governor and police urge calm after malls put up fences over unrest fears
stories.summary: Governor Pramono Anung and Jakarta police called for calm after several shopping malls erected fencing that was widely reported as a precaution against possible unrest. Officials said there was no specific threat behind the move.

stories.headline: Moscow mayor calls deadly restaurant bombing a 'terrorist act'
stories.summary: Moscow's mayor described Saturday's explosion at a restaurant near Kudrinskaya Square in central Moscow as a terrorist act. Officials say three people were killed, including the woman who carried the device, and about 15 were injured. No group has claimed responsibility.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: A heavy day for jobs and workplace news: a 23-year-old worker was killed when scaffolding collapsed at a Jurong Port site, and Toyota distributor Borneo Motors began laying off staff. ICA is warning of very heavy checkpoint traffic for the National Day long weekend, and Parliament sits tomorrow on Maju Forest, Gillman Barracks and the GovTech retrenchments. Lighter notes: a critically endangered langur reappeared at Bukit Timah after 39 years.

stories.headline: Worker, 23, dies after scaffolding collapses on lorry at Jurong Port construction site
stories.summary: A 23-year-old worker was killed when scaffolding collapsed onto a lorry at a construction site at Jurong Port. Both CNA and The Straits Times reported the death on Monday evening.

stories.headline: Toyota distributor Borneo Motors lays off workers in restructuring exercise
stories.summary: Borneo Motors, the local distributor for Toyota and Lexus, has laid off staff as part of a restructuring exercise, CNA and The Straits Times reported. The retrenchments add to a run of job-cut announcements in Singapore over recent weeks.

stories.headline: Roadside parking payment via on-board unit starts for 1,000 trial users
stories.summary: Motorists in a 1,000-user trial can now pay for roadside parking through their vehicle's on-board unit, The Straits Times reported. The trial is a step toward moving roadside parking payment onto the OBU alongside ERP charges.

stories.headline: Government removes contact details of most public officers from online directory amid scam surge
stories.summary: Singapore has stripped the contact details of most public officers from the Singapore Government Directory Interactive (SGDI) after a rise in scams and phishing that impersonated officers. Members of the public are directed to agency hotlines and general enquiry channels instead.

stories.headline: More rental housing options being studied as demand from young Singaporeans grows
stories.summary: Authorities are studying additional rental housing options in response to growing demand from younger Singaporeans, The Straits Times reported. The review comes as more young adults look to move out before they are eligible for or able to buy a flat.

stories.headline: Record low gap between births and deaths poses a demographic challenge
stories.summary: The gap between births and deaths in Singapore has narrowed to a record low, The Straits Times reported, pointing to a population that is ageing faster than it is replacing itself. The trend has direct implications for the workforce, healthcare demand and long-term fiscal planning.

stories.headline: All existing MRT lines to get overheating axle-box detection by 2028
stories.summary: Every existing MRT line will be fitted with a system to detect overheating train axle boxes by 2028, The Straits Times reported. Overheating axle boxes have featured in past rail incidents, and the detection systems are intended to flag problems before they cause a breakdown.

stories.headline: Parliament sits on Aug 4 on Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks housing plans and GovTech layoffs
stories.summary: Tuesday's parliamentary sitting will cover the proposed housing developments at Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks, and the recent GovTech retrenchments. The Workers' Party will also table a motion setting out its vision for an "economy of the future" for all Singaporeans.

stories.headline: ICA warns of very heavy traffic at land checkpoints over the National Day long weekend
stories.summary: The Immigration & Checkpoints Authority expects very heavy traffic at the Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints over the National Day long weekend. Travellers are advised to check traffic conditions before setting off and to allow significantly more time for the crossing.

stories.headline: Man jailed 21 years with caning for repeated sexual abuse of his 13-year-old niece
stories.summary: A man was sentenced to 21 years' jail and caning for repeatedly raping his 13-year-old niece over almost two years. Both CNA and The Straits Times covered the sentencing.

stories.headline: Woodlands Hospice opens, with plans for 70 beds serving the north
stories.summary: Woodlands Hospice has opened and plans to grow to 70 beds to meet palliative care needs in northern Singapore, The Straits Times reported. Demand for palliative care is rising as the population ages.

stories.headline: Critically endangered Raffles' banded langur spotted at Bukit Timah Nature Reserve after 39 years
stories.summary: A Raffles' banded langur, a critically endangered primate found only in Singapore and parts of southern Johor, has been sighted at Bukit Timah Nature Reserve for the first time in 39 years, The Straits Times reported. The species' small population is concentrated in the Central Catchment Nature Reserve.

stories.headline: Massive Attack hit back after being barred from Singapore over Palestinian flag display
stories.summary: British band Massive Attack responded publicly after Singapore authorities barred the duo from returning, following a Palestinian flag display and chants at their 29 July concert at The Star Theatre. Police and the IMDA, in consultation with the Attorney-General's Chambers, issued stern warnings over offences under the Foreign National Emblems (Control of Display) Act and the Public Order Act. The band says its touring party was questioned after the show.

stories.headline: Car-sharing firm GetGo warns of penalties after kids filmed standing through a sunroof
stories.summary: Car-sharing operator GetGo has warned of penalties for unsafe driving after footage circulated of children standing up through the sunroof of one of its cars. The firm said such behaviour breaches its terms of use.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Ukraine is doing the escalating: a second straight day of deep drone strikes hit a Wildberries logistics hub in Vladimir Oblast and a Belgorod university, after claimed hits on the Saratov refinery and Engels bomber base. On Iran the picture is muddled — Trump says talks began Monday, Tehran denies it. In Gaza the disarmament framework is stalling, with strikes into a third day and Israel now formally objecting to the plan.

theatres.name: Russia–Ukraine War
theatres.status: Escalating, with Ukraine's long-range drone campaign the most visible half. Its latest strikes hit a Wildberries logistics centre in Vladimir Oblast and a university in Belgorod, a day after claimed hits on the Saratov refinery and the Engels bomber airfield. Russia says it intercepted 635 drones; Russian governors report at least eight killed. All battlefield claims from both sides remain independently unverified.

timeline.event: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.
Poland's prime minister said a missile that left a crater deep inside Poland was probably Russian.
Russian missiles struck Kyiv and its suburbs early on 1 August. Ukrainian authorities said at least 10 people were killed, and Kyiv renewed its appeal for Patriot interceptors.

A device carried by a woman detonated near a restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square in central Moscow, killing three including the woman and injuring about 15. Moscow's mayor later called it a terrorist act; no group has claimed responsibility.

Ukraine's General Staff said overnight drone strikes hit the Saratov oil refinery, the Engels strategic bomber airfield and a fuel depot in Kaluga region. Russian governors reported at least eight killed; Russia's defence ministry said 635 drones were intercepted.

Ukrainian drones struck a Wildberries logistics centre at Khryastovo in Vladimir Oblast and Belgorod State Technological University, where Russian drones are developed and tested. Wildberries confirmed a fire; Vladimir Oblast governor Alexander Avdeyev said two people were injured.

theatres.name: US / Israel–Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Paused militarily but diplomatically contradictory. Trump says he cancelled planned strikes and that talks were to begin on Monday 3 August with no deadline; Iran publicly denies any negotiations were agreed. US embassies across the region continue to advise Americans to consider departing.

timeline.event: US embassies across the Middle East urged American citizens to "consider departing" the region as Iran threatened further maritime choke points.
Trump said he would hold off on a fresh attack on Iran "subject to being able to rapidly make a deal", claiming Iran and other regional states had asked him not to strike.
Iranian state-linked media denied Trump's claim that Tehran had asked the US not to strike.
Trump, speaking aboard Air Force One, said talks with Iran would take place on Monday but set no deadline for a deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran denied Trump's claim that new talks would begin on Monday, leaving the two sides publicly at odds over whether negotiations exist at all.

theatres.name: Israel–Gaza / West Bank / Lebanon
theatres.status: The disarmament framework is stalling while strikes continue. Palestinian health officials report at least 18 killed in a third consecutive day of Israeli strikes, and Israel has now conveyed formal concerns to Washington about the plan. Hamas says Israel must halt attacks and pull back before handing over weapons.

timeline.event: Hamas-led gunmen attacked southern Israel, killing about 1,200 people and taking roughly 250 hostages, triggering the Gaza war.
Trump announced that the Board of Peace had agreed a framework for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas alongside a phased Israeli withdrawal from Gaza.
An Israeli official said troops would not pull back in Gaza without "genuine" Hamas disarmament.
Hamas said Israel must stop its attacks in Gaza and pull troops back, in line with other terms of the deal, before it hands weapons to a new Palestinian body.
The UN said Israeli demolitions in southern Lebanon were "deeply concerning".

Palestinian health officials said Israeli air strikes across Gaza killed at least 18 people, the third straight day of strikes since the disarmament framework was announced. Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen said no agreement obliges Israel to halt attacks.
Israel conveyed formal concerns to the United States over the Gaza disarmament and withdrawal plan.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: DR Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic is now the country's largest ever and still growing: WHO's 1 August update counts 3,626 confirmed cases and 1,589 deaths, with 1,481 cases added in two weeks and transmission active in 33 of 49 health zones. WHO rates the DR Congo risk very high; an emergency committee meets 18 August. In the US, the Taco Bell-linked Cyclospora outbreak stands at 1,947 cases, no deaths.

outbreaks.name: Bundibugyo Ebola — DR Congo, Uganda & France
outbreaks.status: Intensifying; WHO rates the risk in DR Congo as very high, with transmission active in 33 of 49 affected health zones
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO-confirmed cases only, as of 30 Jul 2026 (WHO Disease Outbreak News 614, published 1 Aug): DR Congo 3,605 confirmed / 1,587 deaths (CFR 44%), Uganda 20 / 2, France 1 / 0. Two DR Congo cases treated in Germany are counted under DR Congo. Since the previous DON on 17 Jul, a further 1,481 confirmed cases and 759 confirmed deaths were reported in DR Congo. Health-worker infections: 151 confirmed, 44 deaths (CFR 29%). 17,863 contacts identified; 654 patients recovered. An IHR Emergency Committee meeting is scheduled for 18 Aug.

outbreaks.name: Cyclosporiasis — United States (imported iceberg lettuce)
outbreaks.status: Traceback points to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico served at some Taco Bell outlets; the product was recalled on 17 Jul
outbreaks.scope_note: CDC multistate outbreak count: 1,947 people infected with Cyclospora who reported Taco Bell exposure, across 9 US states (IL, IN, KS, KY, MI, OH, OK, PA, WV), at least 98 hospitalisations, no deaths. Illness onsets run 22 Jun to 20 Jul 2026. The "countries" figure here counts US states, not countries. Separately, CDC surveillance logs about 6,707 lab-confirmed domestically acquired cyclosporiasis cases nationwide in 2026 from all sources — a much wider tally that should not be confused with this outbreak. CDC's own pages were unreachable this run; these figures are as last reported by CDC and are now over a week old.

stories.headline: WHO: DR Congo Ebola outbreak is now the country's largest on record and still growing
stories.summary: WHO's Disease Outbreak News published on 1 August reports 3,626 confirmed Bundibugyo virus cases and 1,589 deaths as of 30 July — 3,605 cases and 1,587 deaths in DR Congo alone, a case fatality rate of 44%. That surpasses the country's 2018–2020 epidemic (3,317 confirmed cases) to become its largest recorded Ebola outbreak. WHO says 1,481 of those cases were added in the two weeks since its previous update, driven partly by expanded surveillance but mostly by genuine spread. There is no approved vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo virus.

stories.headline: Ituri province accounts for 88% of DR Congo's confirmed Ebola cases as response struggles with insecurity
stories.summary: WHO says Ituri province accounts for 88% of DR Congo's confirmed cases (3,176 of 3,605) and 82.6% of deaths, with Bunia, Rwampara and Mongbwalu the worst-hit health zones. Some 17,863 contacts have been identified, but active follow-up rates range from 66% to 81% by province. The response is running in a conflict-affected setting where insecurity and attacks on health facilities have restricted access for teams and disrupted surveillance.

stories.headline: Could a cyclosporiasis outbreak happen in Singapore?
stories.summary: The Straits Times examines whether the US Cyclospora outbreak linked to imported iceberg lettuce could be repeated here, looking at Singapore's produce import sources, testing regime and how the parasite behaves. Cyclospora spreads through contaminated fresh produce and water rather than person to person.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Two things to act on first: N-able says attackers are taking over N-central servers because its original patch didn't hold, so MSPs need build 2026.3.1.7 now; and Adobe Campaign Classic carries a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated code-execution flaw. The AI supply chain keeps widening — Hugging Face's Diffusers runs attacker code even with trust_remote_code off. Also notable: a Coldcard wallet RNG bug tied to a nine-figure Bitcoin theft.

stories.headline: Chinese threat actor uses leaked DarkSword kit to deploy GHOSTBLADE spyware on iOS
stories.summary: An unidentified Chinese-speaking actor is running a campaign against Apple iOS devices using the DarkSword exploit kit, whose source code leaked publicly on GitHub in March 2026. DarkSword chains six vulnerabilities across two exploit paths and drops GHOSTBLADE, which harvests messages, call history, location, Wi-Fi passwords, browser history, health records and crypto wallet data. Apple has shipped patches for the chain; devices left on older iOS builds remain exposed.

stories.headline: Thermo Fisher patches flaw that could make DNA file tampering nearly undetectable
stories.summary: Thermo Fisher's 31 July bulletin describes a flaw allowing near-undetectable modification of .fsa and .hid output files from Applied Biosystems genetic analysers used in forensic labs, if laboratory controls are circumvented. Five supported product lines get updates that add digital signatures; three end-of-life data collection products will not be fixed. Researchers say the weakness likely existed in crime-lab output since 1995 and that they found no way to detect prior tampering. Disclosure was coordinated with CISA.

stories.headline: N-able says attackers are taking over N-central servers after its first fix proved incomplete
stories.summary: N-able says attackers exploited an authentication bypass in its N-central remote monitoring platform to gain administrative access and reach customer endpoints managed through those servers. The original patch for CVE-2026-18556 did not block a second exploitation path, tracked as CVE-2026-18577, which affects builds before 2026.3.1.7 — shipped on 2 August. N-able reports attackers used Take Control to reach endpoints and registered Cloudflare tunnels as persistent services, which need no inbound firewall rule. NVD scores both issues 8.2 (CVSS v4.0); neither appears in CISA's KEV catalog as of its 29 July release.

stories.headline: Hugging Face Diffusers flaws let model repositories run code despite trust_remote_code being off
stories.summary: Three high-severity issues in Hugging Face's Diffusers library, grouped under CVE-2026-44513 and dubbed "FaceHugger", let a crafted model repository execute arbitrary Python during common loading paths even when the trust_remote_code safeguard is disabled. Versions before 0.38.0 are affected. Because Diffusers is embedded in production ML pipelines, CI/CD systems and container images, a single poisoned repo reaches well beyond the developer's laptop.

stories.headline: Coldcard hardware wallet RNG flaw linked to a nine-figure Bitcoin theft
stories.summary: A random-number-generation error in Coldcard firmware caused ngu.random to fall back to MicroPython's deterministic Yasmarang generator instead of the STM32 hardware RNG, letting an attacker regenerate wallet seeds offline and match them against blockchain addresses. BleepingComputer puts the associated losses at about US$88.6 million (1,367 BTC) drained from 4,585 addresses in roughly 41 minutes; The Hacker News reported a lower figure of about US$70 million. Affected: Mk2/Mk3 firmware 4.0.1–4.1.9, Mk4/Mk5 before 5.6.0 (Edge 6.6.0X) and Q before 1.5.0Q (Edge 6.6.0QX).

stories.headline: Rails patches critical Active Storage flaw with remote code execution potential
stories.summary: Active Storage does not disable libvips handlers, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to read arbitrary files from a Rails application where libvips image processing is enabled and untrusted image uploads are accepted — escalating to remote code execution if cryptographic credentials are exposed. Fixed in Active Storage 7.2.3.2, 8.0.5.1 and 8.1.3.1; libvips should also be at 8.13 or later. Rails 6.x is affected only where Active Storage is configured outside defaults. NVD scores it 9.5 (CVSS v4.0).

stories.headline: Adobe Campaign Classic CVSS 10.0 flaw allows code execution with no user interaction
stories.summary: An incorrect-authorization flaw in Adobe Campaign Classic, rated the maximum CVSS 10.0 by NVD, lets an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code without user interaction. Advisory APSB26-114 carries Adobe's priority-1 rating and covers ACC v7.4.3 build 9397 and earlier on Windows and Linux, affecting on-premise deployments and the on-premise components of hybrid ones; build 9398 fixes it. The same update addresses CVE-2026-48448 (CVSS 8.6), an SQL injection enabling arbitrary file reads. Adobe says it is not aware of exploitation in the wild.

stories.headline: Hijacked hotel Wi-Fi pushes fake software updates to deliver surveillance malware
stories.summary: Attackers are compromising hotel Wi-Fi networks and injecting bogus software-update prompts into guests' browsing sessions, delivering surveillance malware to travellers who accept them. The technique targets people working away from their corporate network, and is a practical argument for always-on VPN and for never installing an update prompted by a captive portal.

stories.headline: Amgen says cloud data breach exposed patient health and proprietary information
stories.summary: Pharmaceutical company Amgen has disclosed a breach of cloud-hosted data that exposed patient health information alongside proprietary corporate material. The company has not published a full scope or a victim count.

stories.headline: Arch Linux disables AUR package adoption to stop a flood of malware
stories.summary: Arch Linux has switched off the ability to adopt orphaned packages in the Arch User Repository after attackers repeatedly claimed abandoned entries and pushed malicious build scripts. AUR packages are user-submitted and built from source on the user's own machine, so a hijacked entry runs attacker-controlled code at install time.

stories.headline: Ad firm Adform's script poisoned to swap crypto wallet addresses across customer sites
stories.summary: Attackers compromised a script served by online advertising firm Adform and used it to substitute their own cryptocurrency wallet addresses on pages across Adform's customer base. It is a textbook third-party script supply-chain attack: every site embedding the tag inherited the malicious code.

stories.headline: Suspected Chinese-speaking hackers target Central Asian governments with OctLurk and SilkLurk
stories.summary: Researchers attribute a campaign against government bodies in Central Asia to a suspected Chinese-speaking group deploying two previously undocumented backdoors, OctLurk and SilkLurk, for long-term espionage access.

stories.headline: Hacker drives DeepSeek via Telegram to attack vulnerable servers autonomously
stories.summary: A threat actor wired the DeepSeek model to a Telegram bot to run largely autonomous attacks against internet-exposed servers, scanning, selecting exploits and following up without step-by-step human direction. It is another data point in a run of incidents this cycle where a general-purpose model is the operator rather than just the tooling.

stories.headline: CISA warns of cyberattacks disrupting US water utilities
stories.summary: CISA has issued a warning about cyberattacks causing operational disruption at US water utilities, following a coordinated campaign that touched more than 30 Minnesota water systems and took one plant offline. Small utilities with thin IT staffing and internet-exposed control interfaces are the recurring weak point.

stories.headline: HollowFrame loader deploys Matryoshka backdoor in spear-phishing attack on a law firm
stories.summary: A targeted spear-phishing campaign against a law firm used a loader dubbed HollowFrame to stage the Matryoshka backdoor. Legal practices are attractive targets because they hold client material that is valuable well beyond the firm itself.
